items.headline: Singapore Airlines posts first quarterly loss since 2022 on fuel and Air India
items.summary: SIA Group swung to a net loss of about S$76 million for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, from a S$186 million profit a year earlier, even as revenue reached a record S$5.71 billion. Net fuel costs jumped 78.5% to S$2.25 billion and its 25.1% stake in Air India added a S$42 million drag.

items.headline: All Singapore households to get extra S$300 in CDC vouchers in January 2027
items.summary: The government unveiled a support package of around S$900 million on 29 July as Middle East tensions raise costs. Every Singaporean household will receive an extra S$300 in Community Development Council vouchers in January 2027, and about 15,200 hawker and market stallholders will get rental support of up to S$1,200.

items.headline: Six men aged 18 to 27 charged with rioting over Yishun carpark assault
items.summary: Six men aged 18 to 27 were charged on 29 July with rioting after a 48-year-old man was punched and kicked unconscious at Block 243 Yishun Ring Road on 24 July. Police arrested seven people aged 18 to 33 between 25 and 28 July; rioting carries up to seven years' jail and caning.

items.headline: No MRT delay over 30 minutes since November 2025, longest run since 2011
items.summary: The Land Transport Authority said there had been no MRT delay of more than 30 minutes since November 2025, excluding the Thomson-East Coast Line — the longest such run since tracking began in 2011. June 2026 was a third straight month with reliability above 2 million train-km between failures, at 2.50 million.

items.headline: Singapore father fined S$5,000 for driving with his two sons on the car boot
items.summary: A 40-year-old man was fined S$5,000 and banned from driving for six months on 29 July after he drove his Porsche with his two young sons perched on the boot. The case drew attention after footage of the drive circulated online.

items.headline: Update: India's Lok Sabha passes tougher anti-paper-leak law with 10-year jail terms
items.summary: The Lok Sabha on 29 July passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, raising maximum jail terms to 10 years, candidate fines to up to Rs 50 lakh and service-provider fines to up to Rs 5 crore, with fast-track trials within three months. It follows the NEET paper-leak scandal that forced the education minister's resignation.

items.headline: India's private-sector activity slows to a four-year low as war and monsoon bite
items.summary: A closely watched flash survey showed India's private-sector activity fell to its weakest in more than four years in July, as the renewed US-Iran conflict lifted oil prices and inflation, with June consumer prices up 4.38%. The Reserve Bank of India maintains that underlying growth remains resilient.

items.headline: Burnham launches social care overhaul but won't rule out an estates 'death tax'
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham on 29 July opened a nine-month national conversation on adult social care, pledging a National Care Service integrated with the NHS and curbs on private-equity ownership. Downing Street declined to rule out a proposed levy on estates — branded a 'death tax' by critics — with no firm funding decision expected before autumn 2027.

items.headline: NHS resident doctors in England stage a five-day strike over pay
items.summary: Tens of thousands of NHS resident doctors in England walked out from 25 July until 30 July in their latest round of industrial action, demanding a 29.2% 'pay restoration'. The British Medical Association blamed Health Secretary Wes Streeting for failing to table a credible offer, and hospitals cancelled thousands of appointments.

items.headline: UK Supreme Court strips Bahrain of immunity in dissidents' spyware case
items.summary: The UK Supreme Court ruled that Bahrain cannot invoke state immunity to block a lawsuit by two Britain-based dissidents, Saeed Shehabi and Moosa Mohammed, who say their devices were hacked with FinSpy spyware. The court held that infecting a device in Britain from abroad is an act committed in the UK, sending the case back to the High Court.

items.headline: Iran fires ballistic missiles at a US air base in Jordan; US says all intercepted
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched at least four ballistic missiles at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on 28 July, in what the United States called an attempted surprise attack. US defences intercepted all of them and no Americans were killed, CENTCOM said.

items.headline: US and Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed militias in eastern Iraq
items.summary: US and Saudi warplanes struck weapons and logistics sites used by Iran-aligned groups across eastern Iraq on the night of 28 July, which CENTCOM linked to a wave of drone attacks. Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces said at least 20 of its members were killed.

items.headline: Powerful earthquake strikes Japan's Kumamoto, killing at least 18
items.summary: A powerful earthquake, measured by the USGS at magnitude 6.8, struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the island of Kyushu on the afternoon of 28 July, killing at least 18 people and injuring dozens, according to Japanese authorities. A shopping mall partially collapsed and a tsunami advisory was issued and later lifted.

items.headline: Uganda declares an end to its 2026 Ebola outbreak
items.summary: Uganda's health ministry declared the country free of Ebola on 28 July, ending an outbreak declared on 15 May that recorded 20 confirmed cases, 18 recoveries and two deaths. The announcement followed the standard 42-day period with no new transmission.

items.headline: Meta and BlackRock form $14 billion venture for a Texas AI data centre
items.summary: Meta and funds managed by BlackRock announced a venture on 28 July to build a one-gigawatt AI data-centre campus in El Paso, Texas, at a cost of about $14 billion. BlackRock's infrastructure arm takes an 80% stake and Meta 20%, with much of the cost funded by debt and operations targeted for 2028.

items.headline: AMD locks up to 2.5 gigawatts of Core Scientific capacity in $14 billion deal
items.summary: Core Scientific said on 28 July that AMD had contracted about 529 megawatts of US data-centre capacity under 15-year leases worth more than $14 billion, with options to reserve up to 2.5 gigawatts in total through 2028. AMD also received warrants for up to 30 million Core Scientific shares.

items.headline: Sam Altman says OpenAI is willing to slow the pace of AI development
items.summary: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the company may have to pace the rate of AI development to give society time to adapt, as OpenAI endorsed a 'Pacing the Frontier' statement signed by more than 1,100 frontier-lab employees calling for an international slowdown mechanism.

items.headline: Fish Audio raises $52 million for expressive AI voice models
items.summary: Voice-AI startup Fish Audio, founded by former Nvidia researcher Shijia Liao, disclosed a $52 million seed round on 28 July, reporting $21 million in annualised revenue and more than 8 million users of its text-to-speech and voice-cloning models in its first year.

items.headline: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady for a fifth straight meeting
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 9-3 on 29 July to keep the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, its fifth consecutive hold, with three officials dissenting as inflation stayed above the 2% target.

items.headline: Dow tumbles more than 1,150 points after the Fed's hawkish hold
items.summary: The Dow closed down about 1,153 points, or 2.2%, at 51,594 on 29 July, the S&P 500 fell 1.5% to 7,316 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.7% to 24,443, after the Federal Reserve held rates and signalled concern that it may be falling behind on inflation.

items.headline: Microsoft tops estimates as Azure pushes annual cloud revenue past $100 billion
items.summary: Microsoft reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $90.0 billion, up 18%, and earnings of $4.81 a share on 29 July, with Azure growth of around 40% lifting its annual cloud revenue above $100 billion for the first time. The shares rose about 3% in after-hours trading.

items.headline: Meta shares fall as AI spending pushes quarterly expenses to $42 billion
items.summary: Meta reported second-quarter revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28%, on 29 July, but earnings of $6.18 a share missed estimates as total expenses jumped 55% to $42 billion and net income fell 14% to $15.8 billion. The shares fell about 6% after hours.

items.headline: Boeing posts a wider quarterly loss on an Air Force One charge
items.summary: Boeing reported second-quarter revenue of $24.6 billion on 171 commercial jet deliveries on 28 July, but a core loss of $0.76 a share — wider than expected — driven by a $280 million charge on the delayed Air Force One programme. Free cash flow was about $0.6 billion.

items.headline: 🎾 De Minaur beats Tsitsipas to open his Washington title defence
items.summary: Defending champion Alex de Minaur beat Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 in the second round of the DC Open in Washington on 29 July, setting up a meeting with Cruz Hewitt.

items.headline: 🎾 Eala rallies past Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen on her Washington debut
items.summary: Filipino Alexandra Eala recovered from a set and a break down, winning seven straight games, to beat Zheng Qinwen 4-6, 6-4, 6-1 on her DC Open debut on 29 July. She next faces defending champion Leylah Fernandez.

items.headline: 🏏 Update: Seales takes five as West Indies beat Pakistan by 90 runs
items.summary: Chasing 211 at Tarouba, Pakistan were bowled out for 120 as Jayden Seales took 5 for 18, giving West Indies a 90-run win in the first Test on 28 July to lead the series. Babar Azam top-scored with 58 not out.

items.headline: 🏎️ Sainz says it is time to decide his future as F1's summer break opens
items.summary: With Formula 1 paused for its summer break before the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort on 21-23 August, Carlos Sainz said it was time to decide his future after a disappointing first season at Williams, as the 2027 driver market began to take shape.

items.headline: LiDAR survey reveals hundreds of lost earthworks from an ancient Amazon society
items.summary: Airborne laser scanning of south-western Amazonia has uncovered nearly 400 monumental earthwork sites built by a little-known society that flourished from about 600 BCE to 850 CE, researchers reported. They estimate the wider region may hold many thousands more such structures.

items.headline: NASA's Psyche probe completes a Mars flyby en route to a metal asteroid
items.summary: NASA released imagery and data from its Psyche spacecraft's Mars gravity-assist flyby, which slingshotted the probe toward the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche while testing its cameras and magnetometer. Psyche is due to reach the asteroid in 2029.

items.headline: Scientists repurpose a DNA-shredding enzyme to kill cancer cells in mice
items.summary: Researchers have engineered the bacterial enzyme Cas12a2 to recognise cancer-linked RNA, such as from a mutated TP53 gene, and then destroy the affected cell's DNA — eliminating tumour cells while sparing healthy ones in mouse experiments, according to a study reported in Nature.

items.headline: A weakening Atlantic current could intensify California's atmospheric-river storms
items.summary: A modelling study finds that a slowing Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation could sharply amplify atmospheric-river rainfall over California by the end of the century, while reducing snowfall over Greenland, by strengthening high-altitude storm-steering winds.

fun_fact.headline: Ketchup was once sold as medicine
fun_fact.body: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was sold as medicine. An Ohio physician, Dr John Cook Bennett, claimed tomatoes could treat ailments such as indigestion, diarrhoea and jaundice, and began selling the extract as concentrated 'tomato pills'. Imitators flooded the market with rival pills until the craze collapsed around 1850.

puzzle.title: The Seventh Floor
puzzle.body: Every workday a man rides the lift from his flat on the 10th floor down to the ground floor and leaves for work. Every evening he returns, rides the lift up to the 7th floor, and walks the last three flights — except when it is raining or when someone else is in the lift, when he rides all the way to the 10th. Why?
puzzle.approach: Nothing is wrong with the lift or the building. The constraint is the man himself — think about what changes on rainy days and when he has company.
puzzle.answer: He is very short. He can reach the ground-floor button going down, but the highest upward button he can reach is the 7th floor. On rainy days he uses his umbrella tip to press the 10th-floor button; when others are in the lift, they press it for him.

word_puzzle.title: Self-Portrait
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange all the letters of each phrase to spell a single word that the phrase also describes. 1. A ROPE ENDS IT (11); 2. DIRTY ROOM (9); 3. IS NO AMITY (9); 4. VOICES RANT ON (12).
word_puzzle.approach: Each phrase uses exactly the same letters as its one-word answer — and, read aloud, slyly describes that answer.
word_puzzle.answer: 1. A ROPE ENDS IT -> DESPERATION; 2. DIRTY ROOM -> DORMITORY; 3. IS NO AMITY -> ANIMOSITY; 4. VOICES RANT ON -> CONVERSATION.
